## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pabbatūpattharajātaka* (Ja 195) is a story in the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana concerning the King of Kosala [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The occasion arose when a minister in the king's service had committed an offense within the royal harem (*antepura*); upon ascertaining the truth of the matter, the king approached Jetavana to consult the Buddha on the appropriate course of action [Fausböll 1879]. The opening verse cited in the commentary begins with the words *Pabbatūpatthare ramme* [Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral records four translations across four languages for this text [SuttaCentral]. No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus likewise records no cross-language alignments meeting the score threshold of 10 [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus does identify Pali-internal text reuse across four segments shared with the second volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0513a2), with the longest aligned passage covering segments §0.4–1.4 [DharmaNexus].
